column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek title or name|English title or name|English text   (English texts of the entries; made from the Greek data)

saint|01-02||Όσιος Σεραφείμ του Σαρώφ|Venerable Seraphim of Sarov|Russian monk of the 18th and 19th centuries. He lived for many years as a hermit in the forest and became known for his kindness and his teaching to those who visited him.
saint|01-03||Προφήτης Μαλαχίας|Prophet Malachi|The last prophet of the Old Testament. His book prophesies the coming of the Forerunner and the Messiah.

saint|01-04||Σύναξη των Αγίων Εβδομήκοντα Αποστόλων|Synaxis of the Holy Seventy Apostles|The Church honors the seventy disciples whom Christ sent out to preach. Many of them became bishops and founded the first Christian communities.
saint|01-05||Αγία Συγκλητική η Οσία|Saint Syncletica the Venerable|Woman of Alexandria in the 4th century. She gave up her wealth and lived as an ascetic, becoming mother and teacher to many nuns.

saint|01-08||Όσιος Γεώργιος ο Χοζεβίτης|Venerable George the Chozebite|Monk of the Judean desert, around the 7th century. He lived at the monastery of Choziba and became known for his humility and asceticism.
saint|01-09||Άγιος Πολύευκτος ο Μάρτυς|Saint Polyeuctus the Martyr|Roman officer who was martyred in Melitene of Armenia in the 3rd century because he did not deny his faith.

saint|01-10||Άγιος Γρηγόριος ο Νύσσης|Saint Gregory of Nyssa|Bishop of Nyssa in the 4th century and brother of Basil the Great. He distinguished himself as a theologian and writer, and contributed to the formulation of the Creed.

saint|01-11||Όσιος Θεοδόσιος ο Κοινοβιάρχης|Venerable Theodosius the Cenobiarch|The founder of cenobitic monasticism in Palestine, in the late 5th century. He organized a large monastery with a hospital, a guesthouse and churches.
saint|01-12||Αγία Τατιανή η Μάρτυς|Saint Tatiana the Martyr|Christian of Rome in the 3rd century, a deaconess of the Church. She was martyred because she refused to sacrifice to the idols.

saint|01-13||Άγιοι Ερμύλος και Στρατονίκος οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Hermylus and Stratonicus the Martyrs|Hermylus was a deacon and Stratonicus his friend in Belgrade. They were martyred around 315 because they did not deny the Christian faith.

saint|01-14||Αγία Νίνα η ισαπόστολος, φωτίστρια της Γεωργίας|Saint Nina, Equal-to-the-Apostles, Enlightener of Georgia|Woman of the 4th century who preached the Gospel in Georgia in the Caucasus and led the king and the people to the Christian faith.

saint|01-15||Όσιοι Παύλος ο Θηβαίος και Ιωάννης ο Καλυβίτης|Venerable Paul of Thebes and John the Hut-Dweller|Paul is the first known hermit of Egypt, of the 3rd century. John the Hut-Dweller lived in Constantinople and became known for his humility.

saint|01-16||Προσκύνηση της Τιμίας Αλύσεως του Αποστόλου Πέτρου|Veneration of the Precious Chain of the Apostle Peter|The Church honors the chain with which the Apostle Peter was bound in prison, from which he was miraculously freed according to the Acts of the Apostles.
saint|01-19||Όσιος Μακάριος ο Αιγύπτιος|Venerable Macarius the Egyptian|Ascetic of the desert of Nitria and Scetis, of the 4th century. He is regarded as the spiritual father of many monks.
saint|01-21||Όσιος Μάξιμος ο Ομολογητής|Venerable Maximus the Confessor|Great theologian of the 7th century. He resisted the teaching of Monothelitism and suffered exile and torture.
saint|01-22||Απόστολος Τιμόθεος|Apostle Timothy|Disciple and co-worker of the Apostle Paul, first bishop of Ephesus. Two of Paul's epistles are addressed to him.
saint|01-23||Άγιος Κλήμης Αγκύρας|Saint Clement of Ancyra|Bishop of Ancyra who was martyred in the early 4th century after many tortures.
saint|01-24||Οσία Ξένη η Ρωμαία|Venerable Xenia the Roman|Woman of Rome in the 5th century. She left her home and lived as an ascetic, known for her humility and hospitality.

saint|01-26||Όσιος Ξενοφών με τη σύζυγό του Μαρία και τους γιους τους|Venerable Xenophon with his wife Maria and their sons|A family of the 6th century that gave up its wealth and devoted itself to monastic life.

saint|01-27||Η Μετακομιδή των λειψάνων του Αγίου Ιωάννου του Χρυσοστόμου|Translation of the Relics of Saint John Chrysostom|In 438 the relics of Chrysostom were brought with honors from exile to Constantinople.

saint|01-28||Όσιος Εφραίμ ο Σύρος|Venerable Ephraim the Syrian|Deacon and hymnographer of the 4th century from Mesopotamia. He wrote many theological and poetic works, and the prayer of the Great Lent is his.

saint|01-29||Η Μετακομιδή των λειψάνων του Αγίου Ιγνατίου του Θεοφόρου|Translation of the Relics of Saint Ignatius the God-bearer|Ignatius was bishop of Antioch and was martyred in Rome around 107. His relics were later transferred to Antioch.
saint|01-31||Άγιοι Κύρος και Ιωάννης οι Ανάργυροι|Saints Cyrus and John the Unmercenaries|Physicians who healed without payment and were martyred in Egypt, in the early 4th century.

saint|02-02||Η Υπαπαντή του Κυρίου|The Presentation of the Lord|Forty days after his birth, Jesus was presented in the temple of Jerusalem, where Simeon and the prophetess Anna met him. The feast is one of the Despotic feasts of the Church.
saint|02-04||Όσιος Ισίδωρος ο Πηλουσιώτης|Venerable Isidore of Pelusium|Monk and writer of the 5th century at Pelusium in Egypt. He left more than a thousand letters of theological and moral content.
saint|02-05||Αγία Αγάθη η Μάρτυς|Saint Agatha the Martyr|Young woman from Catania in Sicily in the 3rd century, who was martyred because she did not deny her faith. She is honored throughout Europe.

saint|02-06||Όσιος Φώτιος ο Μέγας, Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινουπόλεως|Venerable Photius the Great, Patriarch of Constantinople|Learned Patriarch of the 9th century, one of the most educated men of Byzantium. He supported the mission to the Slavs.
saint|02-07||Όσιος Παρθένιος, επίσκοπος Λαμψάκου|Venerable Parthenius, Bishop of Lampsacus|Bishop of the 4th century who became known for his kindness and his care for the poor.
saint|02-08||Άγιος Θεόδωρος ο Στρατηλάτης|Saint Theodore the General|Military leader of Heraclea Pontica, who was martyred around 319. He is honored as one of the great military saints.
saint|02-09||Άγιος Νικηφόρος ο Μάρτυς|Saint Nicephorus the Martyr|Christian of Antioch, who was martyred in the 3rd century. He is known for the forgiveness he showed toward his friend.
saint|02-12||Άγιος Μελέτιος, Αρχιεπίσκοπος Αντιοχείας|Saint Meletius, Archbishop of Antioch|Bishop of Antioch in the 4th century and president of the Second Ecumenical Council (381), where he died.
saint|02-13||Όσιος Μαρτινιανός|Venerable Martinian|Hermit of the 5th century in Palestine, who became known for his severe asceticism.
saint|02-14||Όσιος Αυξέντιος|Venerable Auxentius|Ascetic of the 5th century near Constantinople, on Mount Skopos. Even emperors visited him to ask for his advice.
saint|02-15||Απόστολος Ονήσιμος|Apostle Onesimus|Slave of Philemon who became a Christian and a disciple of the Apostle Paul. Paul's epistle to Philemon refers to him.

saint|02-16||Άγιος Πάμφιλος και οι σύν αυτώ μάρτυρες|Saint Pamphilus and the Martyrs with him|Pamphilus was a presbyter of Caesarea and a great scholar of the Holy Scriptures. He was martyred in 309 together with other Christians.
saint|02-17||Άγιος Θεόδωρος ο Τήρων|Saint Theodore the Recruit|Soldier of the Roman army who was martyred in Amasea of Pontus around 306. According to tradition he saved the city from a great danger.

saint|02-18||Άγιος Λέων, Πάπας Ρώμης|Saint Leo, Pope of Rome|Bishop of Rome in the 5th century. He stood against Attila and contributed to the formulation of the faith at the Fourth Ecumenical Council.

saint|02-19||Απόστολοι Άρχιππος και Φιλήμων|Apostles Archippus and Philemon|Disciples of the Apostle Paul from Colossae in Phrygia. Philemon hosted the first church of the city and was martyred together with his wife Apphia.
saint|02-20||Άγιος Λέων, επίσκοπος Κατάνης|Saint Leo, Bishop of Catania|Bishop of Catania in Sicily in the 8th century, known for his charity and love for the poor.

saint|02-21||Άγιος Ευστάθιος, Αρχιεπίσκοπος Αντιοχείας|Saint Eustathius, Archbishop of Antioch|Bishop of Antioch and a leading figure of the First Ecumenical Council (325) against Arius. He was exiled for his faith.

saint|02-22||Η εύρεση των λειψάνων των εν τοις Ευγενίου μαρτύρων|Finding of the Relics of the Martyrs in the Quarter of Eugenius|The Church celebrates the finding of the relics of Christian martyrs, which took place in Constantinople.
saint|02-23||Άγιος Πολύκαρπος, επίσκοπος Σμύρνης|Saint Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna|Disciple of the Apostle John and bishop of Smyrna. He was martyred around 155 at over eighty years of age.

saint|02-25||Άγιος Ταράσιος, Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινουπόλεως|Saint Tarasius, Patriarch of Constantinople|Patriarch of the 8th century. He presided at the Seventh Ecumenical Council (787), which restored the veneration of icons.
saint|02-26||Όσιος Πορφύριος, επίσκοπος Γάζης|Venerable Porphyry, Bishop of Gaza|Bishop of Gaza around 400, who confronted the idols of the city and closed them with the help of the emperor.
saint|02-27||Όσιος Προκόπιος ο Δεκαπολίτης|Venerable Procopius the Decapolite|Monk and confessor of the 8th century, who resisted iconoclasm and was martyred in Constantinople.
saint|02-28||Όσιος Βασίλειος ο Ομολογητής|Venerable Basil the Confessor|Abbot of the 8th century, who was tortured and exiled because he defended the icons.

saint|02-29||Όσιος Κάσσιανος ο Ρωμαίος|Venerable Cassian the Roman|Monk of the 4th and 5th centuries, founder of monasteries in Marseille. His writings spread to the West as well, and he is honored by the Churches of both traditions.

saint|03-02||Όσιος Νικόλαος ο Πλανάς|Venerable Nicholas Planas|Nicholas Planas (1851–1932) was a priest of Athens, known for his gentleness and charity. He was proclaimed a saint by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 1992.

saint|03-03||Άγιοι Εύτροπιος, Κλεόνικος και Βασιλίσκος|Saints Eutropius, Cleonicus and Basiliscus|Soldiers who were martyred in Pontus in the 4th century. Accounts of their tortures were preserved in the tradition of Amasea.

saint|03-04||Όσιος Γεράσιμος ο Ιορδανίτης|Venerable Gerasimus of the Jordan|Ascetic of the 5th century in the desert of the Jordan, founder of a monastery. According to tradition, a lion followed him.
saint|03-05||Άγιος Κόνων ο Μάρτυς|Saint Conon the Martyr|Christian of Pamphylia, who was martyred in the mid 3rd century, at Magydos.

saint|03-06||Οι Άγιοι Τεσσαράκοντα Δύο Μάρτυρες του Αμορίου|The Holy Forty-Two Martyrs of Amorium|Soldiers and officials who were captured by the Arabs in 838 and put to death seven years later because they refused to change their religion.
saint|03-07||Οι Άγιοι Μάρτυρες της Χερσώνος|The Holy Martyrs of Cherson|Bishops who were sent to Cherson in Crimea to preach the Gospel and were martyred in the early 4th century.
saint|03-08||Όσιος Θεοφύλακτος, επίσκοπος Νικομηδείας|Venerable Theophylact, Bishop of Nicomedia|Bishop of the 8th century, who was exiled in the time of iconoclasm because he defended the icons.

saint|03-09||Οι Άγιοι Τεσσαράκοντα Μάρτυρες της Σεβαστείας|The Holy Forty Martyrs of Sebaste|Soldiers who were martyred around 320 in Armenia, left to freeze on a lake because they did not deny Christ.
saint|03-10||Άγιος Κόδρατος και οι σύν αυτώ μάρτυρες|Saint Quadratus and the Martyrs with him|Christians of Corinth in the 3rd century who were martyred in the time of the persecutions.

saint|03-11||Άγιος Σωφρόνιος, Πατριάρχης Ιεροσολύμων|Saint Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem|Patriarch of the 7th century, who resisted the heresy of Monothelitism and surrendered Jerusalem to the caliph Omar.
saint|03-12||Όσιος Θεοφάνης ο Ομολογητής|Venerable Theophanes the Confessor|Abbot of the monastery of Megas Agros in the 9th century. He was tortured and exiled for the defense of the icons.

saint|03-13||Η Μετακομιδή των λειψάνων του Αγίου Νικηφόρου, Πατριάρχη Κωνσταντινουπόλεως|Translation of the Relics of Saint Nicephorus, Patriarch of Constantinople|The relics of Nicephorus, who died in exile for the defense of the icons, were brought with honors to Constantinople in 846.
saint|03-14||Όσιος Βενέδικτος|Venerable Benedict|Founder of Western monasticism, who lived in the 6th century in Italy. His Rule became a model for the monasteries of the West.

saint|03-15||Άγιος Αγάπιος και οι σύν αυτώ επτά μάρτυρες|Saint Agapius and the Seven Martyrs with him|A group of Christians who were martyred in Palestine, in the years of the persecution of Diocletian.

saint|03-18||Άγιος Κύριλλος, Αρχιεπίσκοπος Ιεροσολύμων|Saint Cyril, Archbishop of Jerusalem|Bishop of the 4th century, known for his Catecheses, which explained the faith to those preparing for baptism.

saint|03-19||Άγιοι Χρύσανθος και Δαρεία οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Chrysanthus and Daria the Martyrs|Couple of Rome in the 3rd century, who were martyred because they became Christians and tried to bring others to the faith.

saint|03-20||Οι Όσιοι Πατέρες που σφαγιάστηκαν στη Μονή του Αγίου Σάββα|The Venerable Fathers Slain at the Monastery of Saint Sabbas|Monks of the monastery of Saint Sabbas in Palestine, who were killed by raiders in the 7th and 8th centuries.
saint|03-21||Άγιος Ιάκωβος ο Ομολογητής|Saint James the Confessor|Bishop of the 9th century who was exiled in the time of iconoclasm.
saint|03-22||Άγιος Βασίλειος, πρεσβύτερος Αγκύρας|Saint Basil, Presbyter of Ancyra|Priest of Ancyra who was martyred in 362 because he openly upheld the faith in the time of Julian.
saint|03-23||Άγιος Νίκων και οι 199 μαθητές του|Saint Nikon and his 199 Disciples|Monk from Sicily in the 3rd century, who was martyred together with his disciples.
saint|03-24||Όσιος Ζαχαρίας|Venerable Zacharias|Ascetic of the 5th century. On March 24 the forefeast of the Annunciation is also kept.
saint|03-26||Σύναξη του Αρχαγγέλου Γαβριήλ|Synaxis of the Archangel Gabriel|The Church honors Gabriel on the day after the Annunciation, because he was the messenger of God.
saint|03-27||Οσία Ματρώνα η Θεσσαλονικιά|Venerable Matrona of Thessaloniki|Woman of the 5th century who served in a family, but left and became a nun in Thessaloniki.
saint|03-28||Όσιος Ιλαρίων ο Νέος|Venerable Hilarion the New|Abbot of the monastery of Pelekete in Bithynia in the 9th century, who became known for his humility and asceticism.
saint|03-29||Άγιος Μάρκος, επίσκοπος Αρεθουσίων|Saint Mark, Bishop of Arethusa|Bishop of the 4th century in Syria, who resisted the idols and suffered tortures.
saint|03-30||Όσιος Ιωάννης της Κλίμακος|Venerable John of the Ladder|Monk of Sinai in the 6th and 7th centuries, who wrote the book "The Ladder" with the thirty steps of the spiritual life.
saint|03-31||Άγιος Υπάτιος, επίσκοπος Γάγγρων|Saint Hypatius, Bishop of Gangra|Bishop of Paphlagonia, a participant in the First Ecumenical Council (325). He was killed by heretics.
saint|04-03||Όσιος Νικήτας ο Ομολογητής|Venerable Nicetas the Confessor|Abbot of the monastery of Medikion in Bithynia in the 8th and 9th centuries. He was exiled because he defended the icons.
saint|04-06||Άγιος Ευτύχιος, Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινουπόλεως|Saint Eutychius, Patriarch of Constantinople|Patriarch of the 6th century and president of the Fifth Ecumenical Council (553).
saint|04-07||Άγιος Καλλιόπιος ο Μάρτυς|Saint Calliopius the Martyr|Christian of Paphos in Cyprus, who was martyred in the 3rd century.

saint|04-08||Απόστολοι Ηρωδίων, Άγαβος, Ρούφος, Ασύγκριτος, Φλέγων και Ερμής|Apostles Herodion, Agabus, Rufus, Asyncritus, Phlegon and Hermes|Members of the seventy disciples, who preached the Gospel in the first churches and are mentioned in the epistles of the Apostle Paul.
saint|04-09||Άγιος Ευψύχιος ο Μάρτυς|Saint Eupsychius the Martyr|Christian of Caesarea in Cappadocia, who was martyred in the years of Julian the Apostate.

saint|04-10||Άγιοι Τερέντιος, Πομπήιος και οι σύν αυτοίς μάρτυρες|Saints Terence, Pompeius and the Martyrs with them|A group of Christians who were martyred in Carthage in North Africa, because they refused to sacrifice to the gods.

saint|04-11||Άγιος Αντίπας, επίσκοπος Περγάμου|Saint Antipas, Bishop of Pergamum|Bishop of Pergamum and martyr, mentioned in the Revelation of John as "my faithful martyr". He is especially honored as the protector against dental problems.
saint|04-12||Άγιος Βασίλειος, επίσκοπος Παρίου|Saint Basil, Bishop of Parium|Bishop of the 8th century on the Hellespont, a confessor of the faith in the time of iconoclasm.
saint|04-13||Άγιος Μαρτίνος ο Ομολογητής, Πάπας Ρώμης|Saint Martin the Confessor, Pope of Rome|Bishop of Rome in the 7th century, who resisted Monothelitism and died in exile in Crimea.
saint|04-14||Απόστολοι Αρίσταρχος, Πούδης και Τρόφιμος|Apostles Aristarchus, Pudens and Trophimus|Co-workers of the Apostle Paul from the early years of the Church. Aristarchus traveled with him.
saint|04-15||Αγίες Βασίλισσα και Αναστασία οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Basilissa and Anastasia the Martyrs|Two women of Rome, who cared for imprisoned Christians and were martyred in the years of Nero.
saint|04-16||Αγίες Αγάπη, Ειρήνη και Χιονία|Saints Agape, Irene and Chione|Three sisters of Thessaloniki, who were martyred around 304 because they kept the holy books and did not deny their faith.
saint|04-17||Άγιος Σίμων, επίσκοπος Περσίας|Saint Simeon, Bishop of Persia|Bishop of Persia and martyr of the 4th century, one of the victims of the persecutions of Shapur II.

saint|04-18||Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Νεομάρτυρας των Ιωαννίνων|Saint John the New Martyr of Ioannina|Young man of Epirus who was martyred in 1526 in Ioannina because he did not deny his Christian faith. He is said to have been a shepherd.
saint|04-20||Όσιος Θεόδωρος ο Τριχινάς|Venerable Theodore the Trichinas|Ascetic of the 4th century in Constantinople, who wore only a hair garment. For this reason he was called Trichinas.
saint|04-22||Όσιος Θεόδωρος ο Σικεώτης|Venerable Theodore of Sykeon|Bishop of Anastasiopolis in Galatia and spiritual father of the 6th and 7th centuries, known for miracles and charity.
saint|04-24||Άγιος Σάββας ο Στρατηλάτης|Saint Sabbas the General|Roman officer of Gothic origin, who was martyred in 272 because he refused to sacrifice to the idols.
saint|04-26||Άγιος Βασίλειος, επίσκοπος Αμασείας|Saint Basil, Bishop of Amasea|Bishop of Amasea of Pontus and martyr of the early 4th century.
saint|04-27||Άγιος Συμεών, επίσκοπος Ιεροσολύμων|Saint Simeon, Bishop of Jerusalem|Second bishop of Jerusalem and relative of the Lord. He was martyred at an advanced age in the years of Trajan.
saint|04-28||Απόστολοι Ιάσων και Σωσίπατρος|Apostles Jason and Sosipater|Two of the seventy disciples. Jason hosted Paul in Thessaloniki. They preached in Corfu, where they are especially honored.
saint|04-29||Οι Άγιοι Εννέα Μάρτυρες της Κυζίκου|The Holy Nine Martyrs of Cyzicus|Nine Christians of Cyzicus who were martyred in the years of the emperor Diocletian.
saint|05-01||Προφήτης Ιερεμίας|Prophet Jeremiah|One of the great prophets of the Old Testament. He lived in Jerusalem at the time of the fall of the city and is known for his "Lamentations".

saint|05-02||Η Μετακομιδή των λειψάνων του Αγίου Αθανασίου του Μεγάλου|Translation of the Relics of Saint Athanasius the Great|The relics of Athanasius, Patriarch of Alexandria, were transferred from Alexandria to Constantinople in the 4th century.
saint|05-03||Άγιοι Τιμόθεος και Μαύρα οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Timothy and Maura the Martyrs|Couple of Egypt, who were martyred in 286. Timothy was a reader and Maura his wife.
saint|05-04||Αγία Πελαγία η Μάρτυς|Saint Pelagia the Martyr|Young woman of Tarsus who was martyred around 287, because she refused to marry Diocletian.
saint|05-06||Δίκαιος Ιώβ ο πολύαθλος|Righteous Job the Long-suffering|Figure of the Old Testament who, despite great trials, kept his faith and patience. He is a symbol of patience.

saint|05-07||Το σημείο του Τιμίου Σταυρού στον ουρανό των Ιεροσολύμων|The Sign of the Precious Cross in the Sky of Jerusalem|In 351 a cross of light appeared in the sky above Golgotha, an event that strengthened the faith of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

saint|05-09||Προφήτης Ησαΐας|Prophet Isaiah|One of the greatest prophets of the Old Testament, who lived in Jerusalem in the 8th century BC. His prophecies about the Messiah are read especially at Christmas.
saint|05-10||Απόστολος Σίμων ο Ζηλωτής|Apostle Simon the Zealot|One of the twelve disciples of Christ. Tradition says that he preached in Egypt, Africa and Persia.

saint|05-11||Άγιοι Κύριλλος και Μεθόδιος, ισαπόστολοι και διδάσκαλοι των Σλάβων|Saints Cyril and Methodius, Equal-to-the-Apostles and Teachers of the Slavs|The two brothers from Thessaloniki created the Glagolitic alphabet and translated the holy books into the language of the Slavs in the 9th century.

saint|05-12||Άγιοι Επιφάνιος, αρχιεπίσκοπος Κύπρου, και Γερμανός, Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινουπόλεως|Saints Epiphanius, Archbishop of Cyprus, and Germanus, Patriarch of Constantinople|Two great hierarchs. Epiphanius (4th century) from Salamis of Cyprus was an important theologian and Germanus (8th century) defended the icons.
saint|05-13||Αγία Γλυκερία η Μάρτυς|Saint Glyceria the Martyr|Young woman of Heraclea in Thrace who was martyred in the 2nd century. Her relics were later transferred to Constantinople.
saint|05-14||Άγιος Ισίδωρος ο Μάρτυς της Χίου|Saint Isidore the Martyr of Chios|Soldier who was martyred on Chios around 251 and is the protector of the island.
saint|05-15||Όσιος Παχώμιος ο Μέγας|Venerable Pachomius the Great|Founder of cenobitic monasticism in Egypt, in the 4th century. He organized monasteries with a common rule and common life.
saint|05-16||Όσιος Θεόδωρος ο Ηγιασμένος|Venerable Theodore the Sanctified|Disciple of Pachomius, who succeeded his teacher in the leadership of the Egyptian monasteries.
saint|05-17||Απόστολοι Ανδρόνικος και Ιουνιάς|Apostles Andronicus and Junia|Paul mentions them in the Epistle to the Romans as "notable among the apostles". Andronicus became bishop of Pannonia.

saint|09-30||Άγιος Γρηγόριος ο Φωτιστής, επίσκοπος Μεγάλης Αρμενίας|Saint Gregory the Illuminator, Bishop of Greater Armenia|Gregory brought the Gospel to Armenia in the 3rd and 4th centuries, and King Tiridates III was baptized by him.

saint|10-02||Άγιος Κυπριανός ο Ιερομάρτυς και Αγία Ιουστίνα|Saint Cyprian the Hieromartyr and Saint Justina|Cyprian was a magician of Antioch, who became a Christian and a bishop. He was martyred together with Justina in 304.

saint|10-03||Άγιος Διονύσιος ο Αρεοπαγίτης|Saint Dionysius the Areopagite|Judge of the Areopagus who became a Christian after the preaching of the Apostle Paul. According to tradition he became the first bishop of Athens.
saint|10-05||Αγία Χαριτίνη η Μάρτυς|Saint Charitina the Martyr|Young woman who was martyred in the years of Diocletian, around 304, in Amisus of Pontus.

saint|10-07||Άγιοι Σέργιος και Βάκχος οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Sergius and Bacchus the Martyrs|Two officers of the Roman army, who were martyred around 303 in Syria. They are honored as protectors of soldiers.
saint|10-08||Οσία Πελαγία η Μετανοούσα|Venerable Pelagia the Penitent|Actress of Antioch in the 5th century, who repented, became a nun and lived on the Mount of Olives.
saint|10-09||Απόστολος Ιάκωβος του Αλφαίου|Apostle James the son of Alphaeus|One of the twelve disciples of Christ. According to tradition, he preached in Judea and was martyred.
saint|10-10||Άγιοι Ευλάμπιος και Ευλαμπία οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Eulampius and Eulampia the Martyrs|Brother and sister who were martyred in Nicomedia in the 4th century, in the years of Maximian.
saint|10-11||Απόστολος Φίλιππος ο Διάκονος|Apostle Philip the Deacon|One of the seven deacons of the first Church. He baptized the Ethiopian eunuch and became bishop of Tralles.
saint|10-12||Άγιοι Πρόβος, Τάραχος και Ανδρόνικος οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Probus, Tarachus and Andronicus the Martyrs|Three Christians who were martyred in Tarsus around 304, after tortures and trials.
saint|10-13||Άγιοι Κάρπος και Παπύλος οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Carpus and Papylus the Martyrs|Carpus was bishop of Thyatira and Papylus a deacon. They were martyred in Pergamum in the 2nd century.
saint|10-14||Οσία Παρασκευή η νέα|Venerable Paraskeva the New|Paraskeva was born in Epivates in Thrace in the 11th century and lived an ascetic life at the Jordan. Her relics are in Iași, Romania.
saint|10-15||Όσιος Ευθύμιος ο Νέος|Venerable Euthymius the New|Monk from Thessaloniki in the 9th and 10th centuries, who lived on Mount Olympus and on Mount Athos.
saint|10-16||Άγιος Λογγίνος ο Εκατόνταρχος|Saint Longinus the Centurion|The Roman officer who, according to tradition, saw the signs at the Crucifixion and said "Truly this was the Son of God".
saint|10-17||Προφήτης Ωσηέ|Prophet Hosea|Prophet of the 8th century BC in the Northern Kingdom of Israel. His book speaks of God's love for his people.
saint|10-19||Προφήτης Ιωήλ|Prophet Joel|Prophet of the Old Testament. His book describes an invasion of locusts and prophesies the descent of the Holy Spirit.
saint|10-20||Άγιος Αρτέμιος ο Μεγαλομάρτυς|Saint Artemius the Great Martyr|Officer of the Roman army who was martyred in 362, under Julian the Apostate, because he accused the emperor.
saint|10-21||Όσιος Ιλαρίων ο Μέγας|Venerable Hilarion the Great|Ascetic of Palestine in the 4th century and disciple of Anthony. He founded monasticism in Palestine and Cyprus.

saint|10-22||Άγιος Αβέρκιος ο Θαυματουργός, επίσκοπος Ιεραπόλεως|Saint Abercius the Wonderworker, Bishop of Hierapolis|Bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia in the 2nd century. His epitaph is among the earliest Christian texts.

saint|10-24||Άγιος Αρέθας ο Μεγαλομάρτυς και οι σύν αυτώ μάρτυρες|Saint Arethas the Great Martyr and the Martyrs with him|Arethas was leader of the Christian community of Najran in Arabia. He was martyred with many others in 523.

saint|10-27||Άγιος Νέστωρ ο Μάρτυς της Θεσσαλονίκης|Saint Nestor the Martyr of Thessaloniki|Young man of Thessaloniki who, according to tradition, helped Demetrius defeat Lyaeus with his prayer, around 306.

saint|10-28||Η Αγία Σκέπη της Θεοτόκου|The Holy Protection of the Theotokos|In Greece the feast of the Protection of the Virgin Mary is celebrated on October 28, the day of the National Anniversary of the "No". The Church asks for the protection (skepi) of the Theotokos.
saint|10-29||Οσία Αναστασία η Ρωμαία|Venerable Anastasia the Roman|Young woman of Rome in the 6th century, who fled to Alexandria and lived as a nun, without becoming known in society.

saint|10-30||Άγιοι Ζηνόβιος και Ζηνοβία οι Αναργύρους|Saints Zenobius and Zenobia the Unmercenaries|Siblings from Aegae in Cilicia, physicians who healed for free, and were martyred in the years of Diocletian.

saint|10-31||Απόστολοι Στάχυς, Αμπλίας, Ουρβανός, Ναρκίσσος, Απελλής και Αριστόβουλος|Apostles Stachys, Ampliatus, Urbanus, Narcissus, Apelles and Aristobulus|Disciples of the Apostles, who are mentioned by Paul in the Epistle to the Romans.

saint|11-01||Άγιοι Κοσμάς και Δαμιανός οι Ανάργυροι της Ασίας|Saints Cosmas and Damian the Unmercenaries of Asia|Two brothers, physicians, who healed the sick without payment. They were martyred in Asia (Asia Minor) in the 3rd century.
saint|11-03||Άγιοι Ακεψιμάς, Ιωσήφ και Αειθαλάς|Saints Acepsimas, Joseph and Aithalas|Christians of Persia who were martyred in the 4th century, in the persecutions of Shapur II.
saint|11-04||Όσιος Ιωαννίκιος ο Μέγας|Venerable Joannicius the Great|Monk from Bithynia in the 8th and 9th centuries, who was first a shepherd and a soldier and became a great ascetic.
saint|11-05||Άγιοι Γαλακτίων και Επιστήμη οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Galaction and Episteme the Martyrs|Spouses from Emesa in Syria, who were martyred in the years of Decius, around 250.

saint|11-06||Άγιος Παύλος ο Ομολογητής, Αρχιεπίσκοπος Κωνσταντινουπόλεως|Saint Paul the Confessor, Archbishop of Constantinople|Bishop of Constantinople in the 4th century, who resisted the Arians and was exiled.

saint|11-07||Οι Άγιοι Τριάντα Τρεις Μάρτυρες της Μελιτηνής|The Holy Thirty-Three Martyrs of Melitene|Soldiers of Melitene in Armenia, who were martyred around 297, together with their leader Leontius.

saint|11-10||Απόστολοι Ολυμπάς, Ρόδων, Σωσίπατρος, Τέρτιος, Έραστος και Κουάρτος|Apostles Olympas, Herodion, Sosipater, Tertius, Erastus and Quartus|Disciples of the Apostles, who are mentioned by Paul in the Epistle to the Romans.
saint|11-11||Άγιος Μηνάς ο Μεγαλομάρτυς|Saint Menas the Great Martyr|Soldier from Egypt, who was martyred around 295, and is especially honored in Crete, as protector of Heraklion.

saint|11-12||Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Ελεήμων, Πατριάρχης Αλεξανδρείας|Saint John the Almsgiver, Patriarch of Alexandria|Patriarch of Alexandria in the 6th and 7th centuries, known for his great charity and support of the poor.
saint|11-15||Άγιοι Γουρίας, Σαμωνάς και Άβιβος οι Ομολογητές|Saints Gurias, Samonas and Abibus the Confessors|Three Christians of Edessa, who were martyred under Diocletian and under Licinius.

saint|11-16||Απόστολος και Ευαγγελιστής Ματθαίος|Apostle and Evangelist Matthew|One of the twelve disciples of Christ and author of the first Gospel. He was a tax collector before becoming a disciple.

saint|11-17||Άγιος Γρηγόριος ο Θαυματουργός, επίσκοπος Νεοκαισαρείας|Saint Gregory the Wonderworker, Bishop of Neocaesarea|Bishop of the 3rd century in Pontus, who was a disciple of Origen. The name "Wonderworker" comes from the many miracles attributed to him.
saint|11-18||Άγιος Πλάτων ο Μάρτυς|Saint Plato the Martyr|Young man from Ancyra, who was martyred in the years of Maximian, in the 3rd century.
saint|11-19||Προφήτης Αβδιού|Prophet Obadiah|Prophet of the Old Testament, author of its shortest book, which contains a prophecy about Edom.

saint|11-20||Προεόρτια των Εισοδίων και Όσιος Γρηγόριος ο Δεκαπολίτης|Forefeast of the Presentation of the Theotokos and Venerable Gregory the Decapolite|Gregory was born in Irenopolis of Isauria and lived in the 9th century. He defended the icons and was known as an ascetic.
saint|11-22||Απόστολοι Φιλήμων, Άρχιππος και Απφία|Apostles Philemon, Archippus and Apphia|Disciples of the Apostle Paul from Colossae in Phrygia. Philemon hosted the first church of the city.

saint|11-23||Άγιοι Αμφιλόχιος, επίσκοπος Ικονίου, και Γρηγόριος, επίσκοπος Ακράγαντος|Saints Amphilochius, Bishop of Iconium, and Gregory, Bishop of Acragas|Two hierarchs, the first of the 4th century, a friend of the Cappadocians, and the second of the 6th century in Sicily.
saint|11-24||Άγιος Κλήμης, Πάπας Ρώμης|Saint Clement, Pope of Rome|Bishop of Rome in the late 1st century and author of an epistle to the Church of Corinth.
saint|11-26||Όσιος Στυλιανός ο Παφλαγών|Venerable Stylianos of Paphlagonia|Ascetic of Paphlagonia in the 6th century. He is regarded as protector of children.
saint|11-27||Άγιος Ιάκωβος ο Πέρσης|Saint James the Persian|James was a soldier in Persia and the son of a Christian family. He was martyred in 421 because he refused to deny Christ.

saint|11-28||Άγιος Στέφανος ο Νέος, μάρτυς της εικονομαχίας|Saint Stephen the New, Martyr of Iconoclasm|Monk from Constantinople, who was martyred in 764 because he defended the icons in the years of Constantine V.
saint|11-29||Άγιος Παράμονος και οι 370 Μάρτυρες|Saint Paramon and the 370 Martyrs|Paramon was martyred with 370 Christians in the years of Decius, around 250.
saint|12-01||Προφήτης Ναούμ|Prophet Nahum|Prophet of the Old Testament in the 7th century BC. His book foretells the fall of Nineveh.
saint|12-02||Προφήτης Αββακούμ|Prophet Habakkuk|Prophet of the 7th century BC in Jerusalem. His book is known for the phrase "the righteous shall live by my faith".
saint|12-03||Προφήτης Σοφονίας|Prophet Zephaniah|Prophet of the Old Testament, of the 7th century BC. His book speaks of the "day of the Lord".
saint|12-07||Άγιος Αμβρόσιος, επίσκοπος Μεδιολάνων|Saint Ambrose, Bishop of Milan|Bishop of Milan in the 4th century. He was a powerful hierarch of the West and teacher of Augustine.
saint|12-08||Όσιος Πατάπιος|Venerable Patapius|Ascetic of Egypt in the 7th century, who lived in Constantinople. A church was founded in his honor.
saint|12-09||Η Σύλληψη της Θεοτόκου από την Αγία Άννα|The Conception of the Theotokos by Saint Anna|The Church celebrates the conception of the Virgin Mary by Anna, according to tradition.
saint|12-10||Άγιοι Μηνάς, Ερμογένης και Ευγραφός οι Μάρτυρες|Saints Menas, Hermogenes and Eugraphus the Martyrs|Three Christians who were martyred in Alexandria in the 4th century.
saint|12-11||Όσιος Δανιήλ ο Στυλίτης|Venerable Daniel the Stylite|Ascetic of the 5th century, who lived on a pillar near Constantinople for thirty-three years.

saint|12-16||Προφήτης Αγγαίος|Prophet Haggai|Prophet of the Old Testament, who encouraged the Israelites to rebuild the temple of Jerusalem after the captivity.

saint|12-18||Άγιος Σεβαστιανός ο Μάρτυς|Saint Sebastian the Martyr|Soldier at the court of Diocletian, who helped imprisoned Christians and was martyred around 288.
saint|12-19||Άγιος Βονιφάτιος ο Μάρτυς|Saint Boniface the Martyr|Boniface was a servant in Rome in the early 4th century. He lived sinfully, but repented and was martyred in Tarsus.
saint|12-20||Άγιος Ιγνάτιος ο Θεοφόρος|Saint Ignatius the God-bearer|Ignatius was bishop of Antioch and was martyred in Rome around 107. His epistles are among the earliest Christian texts.
saint|12-21||Αγία Ιουλιανή η Μάρτυς|Saint Juliana the Martyr|Young woman who was martyred in Nicomedia, around 305, because she refused to marry a pagan.

saint|12-22||Αγία Αναστασία η Φαρμακολύτρια|Saint Anastasia the Deliverer from Potions|Young woman of Rome who was martyred in the years of Diocletian, and healed imprisoned Christians. She is called "Deliverer from Potions" because she delivered people from poisons.

saint|12-23||Οι Άγιοι Δέκα Μάρτυρες της Κρήτης|The Holy Ten Martyrs of Crete|Ten Christians who were martyred in Gortyna of Crete in 250, in the years of Decius. They are especially honored as protectors of the island.

saint|12-28||Οι Άγιοι Είκοσι Χιλιάδες Μάρτυρες της Νικομήδειας|The Holy Twenty Thousand Martyrs of Nicomedia|According to tradition, Christians who were martyred in Nicomedia when Diocletian burned the church where they had gathered, in 303.
saint|12-30||Αγία Ανυσία η Μάρτυς|Saint Anysia the Martyr|Young woman of Thessaloniki who was martyred in 304, after refusing to sacrifice to the gods.
saint|12-31||Οσία Μελάνη η Ρωμαία|Venerable Melania the Roman|Wealthy Roman woman who distributed her property to the poor and became a nun in Jerusalem, in the 5th century.

According to local tradition they belong to the three hundred saints who came to the island.

saint|09-07||Όσιος Σωζόμενος ο Κύπριος|Venerable Sozomenos the Cypriot|Sozomenos practiced asceticism in the region of Galata in Cyprus, where there is a monastery bearing his name. His memory is celebrated by the Church of Cyprus on 7 September.

saint|10-17||Άγιος Λάζαρος ο τετραήμερος, Επίσκοπος Κιτίου|Saint Lazarus the Four-days-dead, Bishop of Kition|Lazarus was a friend of Christ and was raised by Him four days after his death. According to tradition he came to Cyprus and became bishop of Kition, present-day Larnaca, where he is honored as the patron of the city.

saint|11-12||Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Ελεήμων, Πατριάρχης Αλεξανδρείας, ο Κύπριος|Saint John the Merciful, Patriarch of Alexandria, the Cypriot|John was born in Amathus, Cyprus, in the 6th century and became Patriarch of Alexandria. He became known for his charity and was called the Merciful. Cyprus honors him as its own saint.

saint|01-01||Άγιος Βασίλειος ο Μέγας, Αρχιεπίσκοπος Καισαρείας|Saint Basil the Great, Archbishop of Caesarea|Basil was born around 330 in Caesarea of Cappadocia and became bishop of the city. He was a great theologian and philanthropist, organized charitable institutions, and died in 379. The Circumcision of Christ is celebrated on the same day.

saint|01-06||Τα Άγια Θεοφάνεια (Φώτα)|The Holy Theophany (Epiphany, the Lights)|The feast commemorates the baptism of Jesus by John in the Jordan River. According to the Gospels, the Holy Trinity was revealed then. On this day the blessing of the waters takes place.

saint|01-07||Σύναξη του Αγίου Ιωάννη του Προδρόμου και Βαπτιστή|Synaxis of Saint John the Forerunner and Baptist|John baptized Jesus in the Jordan and preached repentance. He is honored as the Forerunner, because he prepared the world for Christ.
saint|01-17||Όσιος Αντώνιος ο Μέγας|Venerable Anthony the Great|Anthony was born around 251 in Egypt and lived as an ascetic in the desert. He is considered the father of monasticism and died in 356.

saint|01-18||Άγιοι Αθανάσιος και Κύριλλος, Πατριάρχες Αλεξανδρείας|Saints Athanasius and Cyril, Patriarchs of Alexandria|Athanasius fought Arianism and is the theologian of the Creed. Cyril, a patriarch later on, defended the title of Theotokos.

saint|01-20||Όσιος Ευθύμιος ο Μέγας|Venerable Euthymius the Great|Euthymius was born in Melitene of Cappadocia in 377 and lived as a monk in the desert of Palestine. He became a teacher of many ascetics and died in 473.

saint|01-25||Άγιος Γρηγόριος ο Θεολόγος|Saint Gregory the Theologian|Gregory was born in Cappadocia and served as Archbishop of Constantinople. He was a poet and orator and died around 390. He is one of the Three Hierarchs.

saint|01-30||Οι Τρεις Ιεράρχες: Βασίλειος ο Μέγας, Γρηγόριος ο Θεολόγος, Ιωάννης ο Χρυσόστομος|The Three Hierarchs: Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian, John Chrysostom|The Church honors the three great teachers together. The day is also the day of Greek Letters, with a school holiday.

saint|02-01||Άγιος Τρύφων ο Μάρτυρας|Saint Tryphon the Martyr|Tryphon was born in Phrygia in Asia Minor and, according to tradition, healed the sick by prayer. He was martyred under Emperor Decius, around 250. He is honored as the patron of vine-growers and gardens.

saint|02-03||Άγιος Συμεών ο Θεοδόχος και Αγία Άννα η Προφήτιδα|Saint Symeon the God-receiver and Saint Anna the Prophetess|The two received the infant Jesus in the temple of Jerusalem, when his parents brought him to dedicate him. Symeon took him in his arms and thanked God.

saint|02-10||Άγιος Χαράλαμπος ο Ιερομάρτυρας|Saint Charalambos the Hieromartyr|Charalambos was bishop of Magnesia and, according to tradition, was martyred in extreme old age under Septimius Severus, around 202. He is honored as a protector during epidemics.

saint|02-11||Άγιος Βλάσιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας|Saint Blaise the Hieromartyr|Blaise was bishop of Sebaste in Armenia and was martyred in the early 4th century. He is honored as the patron of animals and livestock breeders.

saint|02-24||Α΄ και Β΄ εύρεση της τιμίας κεφαλής του Αγίου Ιωάννη του Προδρόμου|First and Second Finding of the Honorable Head of Saint John the Forerunner|The feast commemorates, according to tradition, the finding of the head of the Forerunner after his beheading. John is honored as the herald of Christ.

saint|03-01||Αγία Ευδοκία η Οσιομάρτυς|Saint Eudocia the Venerable Martyr|Eudocia came from Heliopolis in Lebanon and, according to tradition, spent her youth in luxury before converting to Christianity. She was martyred in the early 2nd century.

saint|03-17||Όσιος Αλέξιος ο άνθρωπος του Θεού|Venerable Alexis the Man of God|According to tradition, Alexis was born into a wealthy family of Rome and left his riches to live as a beggar and ascetic. He is honored as "the Man of God".

saint|03-25||Ο Ευαγγελισμός της Θεοτόκου|The Annunciation of the Theotokos|The archangel Gabriel brings the Virgin Mary the message that she will bear the Son of God. The feast is celebrated nine months before Christmas and coincides with the national holiday of 25 March.

saint|04-01||Οσία Μαρία η Αιγυπτία|Venerable Mary of Egypt|According to her life, Mary lived an unsettled life in Alexandria, but after a visit to Jerusalem she repented and lived alone for many years in the desert of the Jordan. She is honored as a model of repentance.

saint|04-04||Όσιος Ιωσήφ ο Υμνογράφος|Venerable Joseph the Hymnographer|Joseph was born in Sicily around 816 and became a monk. He wrote many hymns of the Church, especially canons, and died in 886 in Constantinople.

saint|04-23||Άγιος Γεώργιος ο Μεγαλομάρτυς και Τροπαιοφόρος|Saint George the Great Martyr and Trophy-bearer|George was a Roman officer from Cappadocia and was martyred in the early 4th century under Diocletian. He is honored as the patron of the army and of shepherds. If Pascha falls after 23 April, his feast is moved to Easter Monday.

saint|04-25||Άγιος Μάρκος ο Απόστολος και Ευαγγελιστής|Saint Mark the Apostle and Evangelist|Mark accompanied the apostles Paul and Barnabas and, according to tradition, wrote the second Gospel. He is considered the founder of the Church of Alexandria.

saint|04-30||Άγιος Ιάκωβος ο Απόστολος, αδελφός του Ιωάννη του Θεολόγου|Saint James the Apostle, brother of John the Theologian|James was the son of Zebedee and one of the twelve apostles. According to the Acts of the Apostles, he was beheaded by Herod Agrippa around 44.

saint|05-05||Αγία Ειρήνη η Μεγαλομάρτυς|Saint Irene the Great Martyr|According to tradition, Irene was the daughter of a pagan ruler and embraced Christianity. She was martyred for her faith in the years of the persecutions. She is especially honored in Greece.

saint|05-08||Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Θεολόγος και Ευαγγελιστής|Saint John the Theologian and Evangelist|John was the beloved disciple of Christ and the brother of James. According to tradition he wrote the fourth Gospel and the Apocalypse. He lived for several years in Ephesus and died in extreme old age.

saint|05-21||Άγιοι Κωνσταντίνος και Ελένη, ισαπόστολοι|Saints Constantine and Helen, Equal-to-the-Apostles|Constantine the Great, emperor of the Roman state, granted freedom of religion to Christians in 313 and founded Constantinople. His mother Helen, according to tradition, found the Precious Cross in Jerusalem.

saint|06-01||Άγιος Ιουστίνος ο Φιλόσοφος και Μάρτυρας|Saint Justin the Philosopher and Martyr|Justin was born in Neapolis in Palestine in the early 2nd century. He was a philosopher who became a Christian and defended the faith with his writings. He was beheaded in Rome around 165.

saint|06-11||Άγιοι Απόστολοι Βαρθολομαίος και Βαρνάβας|Saints Bartholomew and Barnabas the Apostles|Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles. Barnabas, a native of Cyprus, accompanied the Apostle Paul on his journeys and is considered the founder of the Church of Cyprus.

saint|06-24||Το Γενέθλιο του Αγίου Ιωάννη του Προδρόμου|The Nativity of Saint John the Forerunner|The Church celebrates the birth of John, who was born to Elizabeth and Zacharias six months before Christ. In Greek tradition the feast is linked with the custom of the Klidonas.

saint|06-29||Άγιοι Απόστολοι Πέτρος και Παύλος|Saints Peter and Paul the Apostles|Peter, a fisherman from Galilee, was the first of the twelve disciples of Christ. Paul, a former persecutor of Christians, became the "apostle to the Gentiles". Both, according to tradition, were martyred in Rome under Nero. The feast concludes the Fast of the Holy Apostles.

saint|06-30||Σύναξη των Αγίων Δώδεκα Αποστόλων|Synaxis of the Holy Twelve Apostles|On the day after Peter and Paul the Church honors all twelve disciples of Christ, who spread the Gospel throughout the world known at the time.

saint|07-01||Άγιοι Κοσμάς και Δαμιανός οι Ανάργυροι (από τη Ρώμη)|Saints Cosmas and Damian the Unmercenaries (of Rome)|Cosmas and Damian were physicians who healed the sick without payment, which is why they were called Unmercenaries. They are honored as patrons of physicians.

saint|07-17||Αγία Μαρίνα η Μεγαλομάρτυς|Saint Marina the Great Martyr|Marina came from Antioch of Pisidia and, according to tradition, was martyred in 304 because she refused to deny Christ. She is especially honored in rural areas.

saint|07-20||Προφήτης Ηλίας ο Θεσβίτης|Prophet Elijah the Tishbite|Elijah lived in the 9th century BC in the kingdom of Israel and defended the worship of the one God. According to the Bible, he was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire. In Greece he is honored in many chapels on mountaintops.

saint|07-22||Αγία Μαρία η Μαγδαληνή, η ισαπόστολος|Saint Mary Magdalene, Equal-to-the-Apostles|Mary from Magdala in Galilee followed Jesus and was among the first people to see the Risen Christ. She is honored as a Myrrh-bearer and Equal-to-the-Apostles.

saint|07-26||Αγία Παρασκευή η Οσιομάρτυς|Saint Paraskeva the Venerable Martyr|Paraskeva was born in Rome in the 2nd century and, according to tradition, was martyred under Emperor Antoninus. She is honored as the patron of the eyes and of sight.

saint|07-27||Άγιος Παντελεήμων ο Μεγαλομάρτυς και ιαματικός|Saint Panteleimon the Great Martyr and Healer|Panteleimon was a physician from Nicomedia and healed the sick free of charge. According to tradition, he was martyred in 305 under Diocletian. He is honored as the patron of physicians and of the sick.

saint|08-06||Η Μεταμόρφωση του Σωτήρος|The Transfiguration of the Savior|Christ goes up Mount Tabor with his disciples Peter, James and John and is revealed before them in brilliant light. The feast is one of the great feasts of the Despotic cycle.

saint|08-15||Η Κοίμηση της Θεοτόκου|The Dormition of the Theotokos|The Church celebrates the death and translation of the Virgin Mary. It is preceded by a fifteen-day fast (Dekapentavgoustos). It is the greatest feast of the Theotokos and one of the greatest of the summer in Greece.

saint|08-29||Η Αποτομή της Κεφαλής του Αγίου Ιωάννη του Προδρόμου|The Beheading of Saint John the Forerunner|The feast commemorates the beheading of John the Baptist on the order of Herod Antipas, following a request by Salome. The day is a strict fast.

saint|09-01||Αρχή της Ινδίκτου (εκκλησιαστική πρωτοχρονιά) και Όσιος Συμεών ο Στυλίτης|Beginning of the Indiction (Church New Year) and Venerable Symeon the Stylite|1 September is the beginning of the Church year. Symeon the Stylite lived in the 5th century in Syria and spent many years on top of a pillar, praying.

saint|09-08||Το Γενέθλιο της Θεοτόκου|The Nativity of the Theotokos|The feast commemorates the birth of Mary to Joachim and Anna, according to the tradition of the Protoevangelium of James. It is the first great feast of the Church year.

saint|09-14||Η Ύψωση του Τιμίου και Ζωοποιού Σταυρού|The Exaltation of the Precious and Life-giving Cross|The feast commemorates the finding of the Precious Cross by Saint Helen in Jerusalem and its elevation before the congregation. It is a day of strict fasting.

saint|09-17||Αγίες Πίστις, Ελπίς, Αγάπη και η μητέρα τους Σοφία|Saints Faith, Hope, Love and their mother Sophia|According to tradition, Sophia was a widow in Rome in the 2nd century and had three daughters. All of them were martyred for their faith under Emperor Hadrian.

saint|09-26||Μετάσταση του Αγίου Ιωάννη του Θεολόγου|Repose of Saint John the Theologian|The feast commemorates the death of John the Theologian in Ephesus, in extreme old age, according to tradition. He was the only one of the twelve apostles who was not martyred.

saint|10-01||Όσιος Ρωμανός ο Μελωδός|Venerable Romanos the Melodist|Romanos was born in Syria in the late 5th century and became one of the greatest hymnographers of Byzantium. According to one tradition he is considered the composer of the Akathist Hymn, which is, however, debated by scholars.

saint|10-04||Άγιος Ιερόθεος ο Αθηναίος|Saint Hierotheus the Athenian|Hierotheus was a disciple of the Apostle Paul and, according to tradition, the first bishop of Athens. Dionysius the Areopagite mentions him as his teacher.

saint|10-06||Άγιος Θωμάς ο Απόστολος|Saint Thomas the Apostle|Thomas was one of the twelve apostles. In the Gospel of John he doubted the Resurrection until he saw Christ. According to tradition he preached the Gospel as far as India.

saint|10-18||Άγιος Λουκάς ο Απόστολος και Ευαγγελιστής|Saint Luke the Apostle and Evangelist|Luke was a physician from Antioch and a companion of the Apostle Paul. According to tradition he wrote the third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles. He is honored as the patron of physicians and painters.

saint|10-23||Άγιος Ιάκωβος ο Απόστολος, ο αδελφόθεος|Saint James the Apostle, the Brother of the Lord|James was the first bishop of Jerusalem. According to tradition, he was martyred in 62 and wrote the Catholic Epistle that bears his name.

saint|10-26||Άγιος Δημήτριος ο Μυροβλύτης και Θεσσαλονίκης|Saint Demetrius the Myrrh-gusher of Thessalonica|Demetrius was a Roman official in Thessalonica and was martyred in the early 4th century. He is the patron saint of the city. His feast coincides with the Demetria, one of the great festivals of Thessalonica.

saint|11-02||Άγιοι Ακίνδυνος, Πηγάσιος, Αφθόνιος, Ελπιδοφόρος και Ανεμπόδιστος, οι μάρτυρες της Περσίας|Saints Acindynus, Pegasius, Aphthonius, Elpidephorus and Anempodistus, the martyrs of Persia|The five saints were Christians of Persia and were martyred in the 4th century, in the persecutions of King Shapur II. The Church honors them together with the many other Christians who were martyred in the same region.

saint|11-08||Σύναξη των Ταξιαρχών Μιχαήλ και Γαβριήλ και των λοιπών Ασωμάτων Δυνάμεων|Synaxis of the Archangels Michael and Gabriel and the other Bodiless Powers|The Church honors the archangels Michael and Gabriel and all the heavenly orders of angels. Michael is regarded as the commander-in-chief of the angelic powers and Gabriel as the messenger of the great revelations.

saint|11-09||Άγιος Νεκτάριος, Μητροπολίτης Πενταπόλεως, ο Θαυματουργός|Saint Nectarios, Metropolitan of Pentapolis, the Wonderworker|Nectarios was born in 1846 in Selymbria, Thrace, with the name Anastasios Kephalas. He served as Metropolitan of Pentapolis, director of the Rizarios School, and founded a monastery on Aegina, where he is especially honored today.

saint|11-13||Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Χρυσόστομος, Αρχιεπίσκοπος Κωνσταντινουπόλεως|Saint John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople|A great orator and hierarch of the 4th century, born in Antioch. He became Archbishop of Constantinople, rebuked the injustices of the powerful, and died in exile in 407.

saint|11-14||Άγιος Φίλιππος ο Απόστολος· αρχή της νηστείας των Χριστουγέννων|Saint Philip the Apostle; beginning of the Nativity Fast|Philip came from Bethsaida and was one of the twelve apostles. The Nativity Fast begins on the day after his feast.

saint|11-21||Τα Εισόδια της Θεοτόκου|The Entry of the Theotokos into the Temple|The feast commemorates, according to tradition, the day when the three-year-old Mary was led by her parents, Joachim and Anna, to the temple in Jerusalem to be dedicated to God.

saint|11-25||Αγία Αικατερίνη η Μεγαλομάρτυς|Saint Catherine the Great Martyr|Catherine was an educated young woman of Alexandria who, according to tradition, was martyred for her faith in the early 4th century. She is especially honored at Sinai.

saint|11-30||Άγιος Ανδρέας ο Απόστολος ο Πρωτόκλητος|Saint Andrew the Apostle, the First-called|Andrew, the brother of Peter, was the first whom Jesus called among the apostles. According to tradition he was martyred in Patras and is the patron of the city.

saint|12-04||Αγία Βαρβάρα η Μεγαλομάρτυς|Saint Barbara the Great Martyr|Barbara was, according to tradition, the daughter of a wealthy pagan from Nicomedia or Heliopolis. She was martyred in the early 4th century. She is honored as the patron of artillerymen and of people who work with explosives.

saint|12-05||Όσιος Σάββας ο Ηγιασμένος|Venerable Sabbas the Sanctified|Sabbas was born in Cappadocia in 439 and founded the Mar Saba Monastery in the Judean desert, which still functions. He died in 532.

saint|12-06||Άγιος Νικόλαος, Αρχιεπίσκοπος Μύρων της Λυκίας|Saint Nicholas, Archbishop of Myra in Lycia|Nicholas was born in Patara in Lycia and became bishop of Myra in the 4th century. He was known for his charity and his miracles. He is honored as the patron of sailors.

saint|12-12||Άγιος Σπυρίδων ο Θαυματουργός, Επίσκοπος Τριμυθούντος|Saint Spyridon the Wonderworker, Bishop of Trimythous|Spyridon was born in Cyprus and was a shepherd before becoming a bishop. He took part in the First Ecumenical Council in 325 and died around 348. His relic is kept in Corfu, where he is the patron saint.

saint|12-15||Άγιος Ελευθέριος ο Ιερομάρτυς|Saint Eleutherius the Hieromartyr|Eleutherius was bishop of Illyricum and, according to tradition, was martyred in the early 2nd century. He is honored as the patron of expectant mothers.

saint|12-24||Αγία Ευγενία η Οσιομάρτυς· Παραμονή των Χριστουγέννων|Saint Eugenia the Venerable Martyr; Christmas Eve|Eugenia was born in Rome and, according to tradition, became a nun dressed in male clothing and was martyred around 258. This day is also Christmas Eve.

saint|12-25||Η Γέννηση του Κυρίου και Θεού και Σωτήρος μας Ιησού Χριστού|The Nativity of our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ|The Church celebrates the birth of Jesus in Bethlehem. The feast has been observed on 25 December since the 4th century and is one of the greatest in the Christian world.

saint|12-26||Η Σύναξη της Υπεραγίας Θεοτόκου|The Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos|On the day after Christmas the Church honors the Virgin Mary, who gave birth to Christ. The feast has existed since the 4th century.

saint|12-27||Άγιος Στέφανος ο Πρωτομάρτυς και Αρχιδιάκονος|Saint Stephen the Protomartyr and Archdeacon|Stephen was one of the first seven deacons of the Church in Jerusalem. According to the Acts of the Apostles, he was the first Christian to be martyred for his faith, stoned by the crowd.
